title: China's gene-editing rules
summary: The regulatory framework that followed the 2018 gene-edited babies case.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

After the 2018 CRISPR pregnancy case, China criminalised unauthorised gene editing and introduced ethics review requirements for human research, with the Criminal Law amendment and subsequent regulations tightening oversight. The rules sit inside a broader biosafety framework and are enforced unevenly across provinces. They shape what Chinese biotech firms can test and what foreign partners will accept.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Mass production
Estimated window 2023–2030
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Regulatory credibility is the practical constraint on Chinese biotech licensing; documented ethics review is now part of the asset.

What Would Change The View

  • Enforcement consistency.
  • Approval pathways for somatic editing trials.
  • International acceptance of Chinese clinical data.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
